authorized_price_tuning.identification: TARGET fixed ex ante and NEVER MOVED across all three sizings: the in-sample 2023-2025 GEOMETRIC-MEAN price bias, +3.4678% (owner-selected estimator, PREREG-neiso104 section 3.1); reproduced from the committed sidecars in this session at 0.034674 and still sized on the declared 0.034678. COEFFICIENT: the pass-through MEASURED ON THE FULL SCORED SPAN by the incumbent keeper's own solve -- the geometric mean of the three in-sample price moves (-5.0592%) divided by the cut that produced them (6.609%) = 0.76550. cut = 0.034678 / 0.76550 = 4.530%. No gate was consulted to choose either number.
authorized_price_tuning.disclosure: THREE THINGS A LATER READER WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE TO DISCOVER, recorded here instead. (1) THIS IS THE THIRD SIZING OF THIS SCALAR (4.53% -> 6.609% -> 4.530%), and PREREG-neiso105 section 3 pre-committed that it would not move again in either direction, calling a third iteration 'a sweep by accumulation'. That lane-level stop rule is OVERRIDDEN FROM ABOVE by the owner direction above, not reasoned away from within. The substance differs from the accumulation that clause feared: the target never moved, no gate was consulted, and what changed is a strictly better measurement of the same physical coefficient (three years with the actual mechanism, versus one year). PREREG-neiso106 section 1 states this at full strength. (2) THE ESTIMATOR OF THE COEFFICIENT WAS ONE CHOICE among three computed before choosing (geometric 0.76550, arithmetic-of-per-year 0.76441, log-elasticity 0.75929); the geometric one is declared because the TARGET is a geometric mean and the two halves of a division must share a geometry. The choice is immaterial -- the three span scalars 0.95433-0.95470, about 0.03% of price against a +/-10% band. (3) 0.95470 IS NUMERICALLY THE SCALAR NEISO-104 DECLARED (0.9547) AND REACHED BY A DIFFERENT, LATER-REFUTED ARGUMENT (an across-year delivered-gas elasticity). It is not that derivation reused: nothing here depends on it. The agreement is itself this lane's finding -- neiso-104's coefficient was sound and its rule-29-prescribed 2025 screen year was the problem, because pass-through tracks delivered gas INVERSELY (1.31 at $1.98/MMBtu down to 0.53 at $6.24) and rule 29 selects the largest-footprint, i.e. highest-gas, i.e. lowest-pass-through year. Filed as an owner ask in PREREG-neiso106 section 7; not acted on by this lane.

disclosures.note: neiso-93 disclosures, reported rather than patched. (a) THE PARASITIC-LOAD CHANGE MOVES THE TUNED YEARS, BY CONSTRUCTION AND ON PURPOSE. The shared parasitic_load_factors file held ZERO NEISO plants in ANY year, 2023-2025 included -- the neiso-92 assessment's '2022-2025 present, 2021 missing' reading is a misattribution of the file's TOTAL row counts, corrected in this session's FINDING SS5. Fixing only 2019-2021 would have left NEISO inconsistent across the span, so the derive covers 2019-2025 and the in-sample years therefore change. That is rule 22's touchpoint loop step 3 (re-train on 2023-2025 around the diagnosed issue), not a side effect, and it is why this re-solve exists. (b) 2019 IS NOT MADE READY BY THIS SESSION, AND A NEW 2019-ONLY BLOCKER WAS FOUND. Pilgrim (EIA 1590) ran Jan-May 2019 for 2.177 TWh before retiring 31 May 2019 and is absent from the EIA-860 operable snapshot the model fleet is built from, so a 2019 solve is short ~2.18 TWh of nuclear REGARDLESS of the extended overlay. Independently visible in EIA-930: Jan-May 2019 telemetry implies a 3,355 MW-fleet CF of 1.18-1.20, impossible, collapsing to a 0.003-0.005 gap from June exactly when Pilgrim stops. 2020-2022 are unaffected. This is a fleet-vintage limitation, NOT fixed here. (c) ONE COMMITTED IN-SAMPLE VALUE WAS CORRECTED BY 1 CENT. The 2025 NYISO_CT_base import rung read 44.48; its own deriver emits 44.47 and always has -- confirmed by re-running the deriver against the PRE-SESSION committed inputs. A hand-transcription slip in the 2026-07-06 paste-in, not an effect of the widening. (d) TWO PRODUCERS COULD NOT BE REPRODUCE-CHECKED AT ALL, and the reason is recorded rather than worked around silently: build_eia860_chp_by_year.py reads release zips this clone does not carry, and the NYISO proxy producer reads damlbmp archives that are gitignored and absent. Both were given a second, equivalent source and the equivalence was then demonstrated on the committed years. (e) THE EIA-930 INTERCHANGE BACK-FILL USED A KEYLESS BULK ROUTE because no EIA_API_KEY exists in this environment. It is EIA's own Grid Monitor six-month CSV archive -- the same family fetch_eia930_bulk_long.py already uses -- and it was shown equivalent to the committed API-sourced extract over 2023-2025 before any new year was taken from it (mean identical to full float32 precision; the only non-identical rows are the DST fall-back hour's two ambiguous rows in opposite order). || neiso-97 DST-REPAIR DISCLOSURE (2026-08-17, audit row O8). This bundle is the incumbent recipe re-solved at the REPAIRED NEISO SMD actual-LMP instrument: the 2018-2023 workbook vintage is DST-naive (flat 24 rows every day) and the committed series was displaced one hour around every DST transition of those years — 562 hub cells, max $40.17/MWh, six fabricated mean cells and one lost hour per year — measured against the market's own daily hourly-LMP reports (0 mismatches, all 9 sheets x both markets x every truth day) and repaired value-preservingly per the PJM input-clock finding's §2a protocol (non-affected cells identical every row; displaced cells == pristine at the corrected offset; the fall-back repeated-hour pair restored from the published daily reports; exactly one NaN per market-year filled with the measured value, zero introduced; 2024/2025/2026 blocks byte-identical). docs/FINDING-debug-b-neiso-smd-clock-2026-08-17.md is the full record. The corrected-clock gate is recomputed at attestation time (this script), not quoted. Blast radius on scoring: bench/NEISO 2023 recomputes; the C3c tail and every determination-bearing criterion status are unchanged. The 2022 validation touchpoint stands as scored on the pre-repair instrument; the NYISO keeper's nyiso_import_hub_prices consumption of this series is filed for the NYISO lane (rule 25), not acted on here. || neiso-99 JOINT DISCLOSURE (2026-08-17, audit row O5 + the Stony Brook routing defect). (1) THE SCORING BASIS MOVES OFF THE ARCHIVED P2 PASS. The incumbent was the only keeper of six that ran, and was RENDERED FROM, P2; this run persists ['P1'] alone. The effect on the means is small (mean lambda -0.0575 / -0.0110 / -0.0378 $/MWh for 2023/2024/2025) but the 2024 ANNUAL MAXIMUM of the max-across-zones price moves $256.93 -> $218.24, i.e. P2 was standing 17.7 % above P1 on that statistic. That is a PRICE-FORMATION statistic and it is reported at full magnitude, not tuned around. (2) THE OUTAGE ROUTING REPAIR. _resolve_unit_group's fac_group short-circuit was a pjm-75 conservatism, not a physical claim, and it handed a liquid-fuel combustion turbine's outage window to a sibling gas bin: plant 6081 Stony Brook's two Diesel Oil CTs (83 MW each, 74 windows each) derated a 305.1 MW combined cycle they are not in for 48.7 % of the 2024 and 56.0 % of the 2025 capacity-year — years in which the CC units 001/002/003 have no windows of their own at all. Three further NEISO plants are affected (1595 Kendall S6, 568 Bridgeport BHB4, 1588 Mystic MJ-1). The discriminator is the unit's OWN primaryFuelInfo and NOT unitType, measured: across all six ISOs 35 CAMPD units filed 'Combustion turbine' sit in a non-CT bin and 27 are GAS-fired members of a genuine block that must keep inheriting it. Extract diff, exact: 3,189 -> 2,932 rows, 0 added, 257 dropped = 236 the fix + 21 reclassified standard->layup in 2019/2020/2026 only, the latter reproduced by a PRE-FIX control re-derivation at HEAD and therefore ambient drift, not this change; within 2023-2025 the ONLY change is the 236 rows and all 2,932 surviving rows are byte-identical on every column. (3) THE ROUTING ARM'S DISPATCH EFFECT IS DOMINATED BY KENDALL, NOT STONY BROOK, WHICH REFUTES THE PREREG'S OWN P3 EXPECTATION AND IS REPORTED AS SUCH: restoring 6081's availability barely moves its dispatch because that block's heat rate 10.6062 sits above 97.5 % of NEISO's CC_REGULAR capacity (cap-weighted p50 7.340) — it is deep out of merit whether or not it is available, the same fact neiso-83 measured at the same plant. (4) CROSS-ISO, FILED NOT ACTED ON (rule 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE]): the same guard would drop mis-routed rows at PJM 593 Edge Moor 10, MISO 2001 New Ulm 7 and 8056 Waterford 4, and NYISO 2516 Northport UGT001. Only NEISO's extract is re-derived here; those are their lanes' calls. (5) THE REPLAY SEAM IS CLOSED IN THE SAME CHANGE: run_replay_bundle and replay_keeper.main rebuilt their kwargs from meta.json AFTER the CLI's P2 gate ran, so commitment=true re-armed the archived pass invisibly on every replay — which is how it propagated across three keeper generations with no operator decision. enforce_legacy_p2_kwargs now gates the RECONSTRUCTED recipe at both entry points and HARD-FAILS rather than silently rewriting it.
